cards.text: This one's a psalm of Asaph, and it opens with God presiding in the divine assembly. Friend, the most serious meeting in my bakery is me versus me deciding chocolate chips or sprinkles, but THIS is a meeting.

cards.question: God presides in the divine assembly, and among the gods He renders ___

cards.text: Then God speaks, and He opens with a question. I bet nobody in that room is relaxed.

cards.question: In the divine assembly, God asks how long they'll keep doing something. What is it?

answers.text: Judging unjustly and favoring the wicked
Ignoring the feasts and the sacrifices
Refusing to hear any cases at all

cards.text: So what should they be doing instead? God tells them.

cards.question: God tells the assembly whose cause to defend. Whose is it?
God also tells the assembly to uphold the rights of the afflicted and oppressed.

cards.text: God also says to rescue the weak and needy and save them from the hand of the wicked.
Then God says, "They do not know or understand; they wander in the darkness…" You ever cross a dark kitchen at night and find EVERY cabinet door with your shin?

cards.question: Along with that wandering in the darkness, what does God say is shaken?

answers.text: All the foundations of the earth

cards.text: Then God brings up something He has said about them. I bet everybody in that room sits up straight.

cards.question: God reminds the ones He's judging what He has said they are. What is it?

answers.text: Gods and sons of the Most High
Priests and servants of the temple

cards.text: Then comes one little word: But. I spent years in a junk drawer hearing "That old stamper still works, but…" so I KNOW what that word does.

cards.question: God called them gods and sons of the Most High. What does He say will happen to them?

answers.text: They will be scattered among the nations
They will be turned into servants

cards.question: Besides dying like mortals, God tells the ones He called sons of the Most High that like rulers they will fall.

cards.text: Then the psalm turns. It stops reporting on the assembly and calls out to God Himself to arise.

cards.question: The psalm asks God to arise and judge only the nation of Israel.
The psalm calls on God to judge the earth. What reason does it give?

answers.text: All the nations are His inheritance
The rulers have all stepped down
The nations have asked Him to
